classification.difficultyReason: Identifies the angle measured below the horizontal at the upper observation point.

content.prompt: Which of the following is the angle of depression?

spec.sourceRegion: Concept Check question 8, lower right column, between questions 8 and 9.
spec.description: Unshaded right triangle with a horizontal base, right vertical side and diagonal rising from the lower-left point to the upper-right point. Filled markers occur at both diagonal endpoints. A dashed horizontal extends left from the upper point and a dashed vertical extends upwards from the lower point. All four source angle labels and the lower-right right-angle square are retained.
spec.mathematics: α is between the upper horizontal reference and the descending sight line; β is between that sight line and the right vertical side. γ is between the base and rising sight line; δ is between the lower vertical reference and rising sight line. Coordinates define drawing proportions only and introduce no stated measurements.
spec.answerVisibility: All four angle labels are permanent givens. No correct-answer highlight or solution annotation is included.

answer.worked: $\alpha$ is measured downwards from the horizontal at the upper observation point, so it is the angle of depression.
